summary:
MartianBound is an interactive Mars mission training simulator designed to make planetary science and space exploration more engaging, accessible, and educational. It addresses the challenge of understanding the complexities of human exploration on Mars through theory alone by allowing users to experience mission planning, resource management, scientific exploration, and decision-making in a simulated Martian environment.

Players take on the role of mission planners, selecting crew members, choosing mission durations, evaluating potential landing regions, and managing essential resources such as oxygen, water, food, and power. Throughout the simulation, they encounter environmental challenges, including dust storms and radiation risks, requiring strategic decisions to keep the mission on track.

Grounded in NASA scientific datasets and Mars research, MartianBound connects real planetary science with interactive learning. Our goal is to inspire students and curious minds to explore the science, teamwork, and critical thinking behind future human missions to Mars.
details:
Project Overview

MartianBound is an interactive Mars mission training simulator developed to make planetary science and future human Mars exploration more accessible through engaging, decision-based gameplay. Instead of simply presenting scientific information, the project allows users to experience the challenges of planning and managing a simulated Mars mission.

How It Works

The experience follows a structured mission workflow. Players begin by selecting their crew and mission duration, then configure mission resources and choose a potential Martian landing region based on its terrain, environmental conditions, and scientific significance.

Once the mission begins, players experience a day-by-day simulation where they must manage essential resources, including oxygen, water, food, and power. They also face environmental challenges such as radiation exposure and dust storms. These situations require careful planning and strategic decisions to maintain mission stability and achieve scientific objectives.

At the end of the mission, players receive a performance report based on their decisions, resource management, and scientific progress.

Scientific Foundation

MartianBound incorporates real Mars research and NASA-related scientific datasets to connect gameplay with planetary science. Our research includes NASA's Subsurface Water Ice Mapping (SWIM) project and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter's SHARAD radar data. These resources help inform the project's approach to understanding Martian subsurface ice and the scientific importance of potential exploration regions.

Development Tools and Technologies

  • Game Engine: Godot Engine 4
  • Programming Language: GDScript
  • Development Environment: Google Antigravity
  • AI Assistance: Claude, ChatGpt
  • UI/UX Design: Figma
  • Visual Design and Presentation: Canva
  • Voice Assistance: ElevenLabs
  • Scientific Research: NASA-related datasets and planetary science resources

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of MartianBound lies in combining scientific research, mission planning, resource management, and interactive simulation into one educational experience. Rather than treating Mars exploration as a simple journey, it presents it as a complex mission where environmental conditions, limited resources, and interconnected decisions influence the outcome.

Factors Considered

During development, our team considered scientific relevance, educational value, gameplay accessibility, resource constraints, and the complexity of real Mars exploration. We aimed to balance scientific accuracy with an understandable and engaging experience, while keeping the project feasible as an initial prototype.

Intended Impact and Future Vision

Our goal is to help students, aspiring explorers, and curious learners better understand the challenges of human exploration on Mars. We want to encourage scientific curiosity, critical thinking, strategic planning, and interest in planetary science.

MartianBound is our first step toward a broader interactive learning experience, with future plans to introduce deeper simulations, richer missions, expanded scientific datasets, and more realistic Mars exploration scenarios.
